_comment: HPE VME CPF provider settings. Every leaf is {value, default, description}: only 'value' is read, 'default' and 'description' are informational and are refreshed by the provider when it migrates this file. See docs/SETTINGS.md.

locations._comment: Where the provider keeps its files. Changes are applied at the next process start, never on a hot reload (in-flight clone tracking lives in these files).

data_directory.description: Folder for the log and state files. Empty = the script folder; a relative path resolves against the script folder.

log_file.description: Log file name, relative to data_directory unless absolute.

clone_state_file.description: In-flight clone tracking. Survives a provider restart.

maintenance_state_file.description: Templates RAS has put into maintenance (guests/convert is_template=false). Survives a restart.

template_state_file.description: Instances RAS marked as templates (template_method 'basic'). The only source of is_template.

former_template_state_file.description: Instances that were RAS templates when RAS sent a delete for them ('Delete Template' in the RAS Console). The provider never deletes these VMs; they stay listed as ordinary guests and can be made templates again.

stuck_clone_state_file.description: Clones the provider gave up on that VME has not finished yet. Each one keeps holding a cloning.max_concurrent_clone_operations slot. Survives a restart.

template_version_state_file.description: template_method 'versioning': each RAS template version's VME snapshot and linked-clone virtual image. Rebuilt from VME (by name) for a version it is missing.

settings_reload_interval_seconds.description: How often this file's last-write time is checked, opportunistically on incoming requests. Range: 5-3600.

connection._comment: VME REST transport. Host and credentials come from the RAS Console (provider/connect), not from this file.

ssl_check.description: Validate the appliance TLS certificate. A per-connection ssl_check in the RAS custom settings overrides this.

use_system_proxy.description: false = connect directly (-NoProxy). true = use the system proxy, including WPAD auto-detection, which can stall a call for seconds.

request_timeout_seconds.description: How long a call may wait for VME to start answering (connect + TLS + server processing). One value for every call: on PowerShell 7.4+ it belongs to the pooled connection, and changing it per call would drop the connection. A clone PUT that exceeds it is tracked as "response lost", never retried. Range: 5-300.

read_timeout_seconds.description: PowerShell 7.4+: longest silence tolerated while a response body is being received (a multi-MB listing page). Older hosts have no separate read timeout. Range: 5-600.

retry_max_attempts.description: Attempts for a GET on no response, HTTP 429 or 5xx. Idempotent writes (power actions, DELETE) get at most 2. A clone PUT is never retried. Range: 1-5.

retry_delay_milliseconds.description: Base delay between retries, multiplied by the attempt number. Range: 0-5000.

retry_after_max_seconds.description: Ceiling on an HTTP 429 Retry-After wait. The provider serves one request at a time, so every second waited delays every other RAS call. Range: 0-30.

oauth_client_id.description: OAuth client id for the password and refresh_token grants.

token_refresh_margin_seconds.description: Refresh a token whose expiry is known this many seconds before it expires. Range: 30-86400.

token_renewal._comment: Proactive renewal of a pre-issued access_token (RAS custom setting) whose expiry is discovered via GET /api/user-settings. Needs a refresh_token.

proactive_enabled.description: Discover the pre-issued token expiry and renew it ahead of time. The reactive renewal on HTTP 401 always stays on.

expiry_check_interval_hours.description: How often the expiry is re-discovered. Range: 1-720.

lead_days.description: Start renewing this many days before the discovered expiry. Range: 0-30.

max_attempts.description: Renewal attempts per expiry cycle. Range: 1-50.

retry_interval_hours.description: Minimum spacing between renewal attempts. Range: 1-72.

capabilities._comment: Advertised to RAS by provider/initialize. can_link_clones is not a setting: it is true exactly when template_method is 'versioning' (VME 9.1+).

guests_polling_rate.description: Seconds between RAS guests/list polls. At 3000 guests one listing is ~18 MB, so this is also the natural refresh cadence of the inventory. Range: 5-600.

tasks_polling_rate.description: Seconds between RAS tasks/get polls for an in-flight clone. RAS learns that a clone finished only at its next poll, so a lower value finishes pool builds sooner. Keep tasks_polling_rate x tasks_polling_retries above cloning.provision_timeout_seconds. Range: 5-300.

tasks_polling_retries.description: tasks/get polls before RAS gives up on a task. CPF documents 0-180. Range: 1-180.

template_method.description: CPF template contract. 'basic': guests/convert marks templates, full clones only. 'versioning': template versions with linked clones (VME 9.1+) -- each version is a VME snapshot plus a linked-clone virtual image, and can_link_clones is advertised. 'none': no templates (guests/convert and guests/clone are refused). RAS reads this at provider/initialize; existing templates may need re-creating after a change. Allowed: none, basic, versioning.

inventory._comment: The in-memory instance inventory that serves guests/list and guests/get. See docs/DESIGN.md.

list_min_refresh_seconds.description: Minimum age of the inventory before a guests/list triggers a new full listing. A guests/list that arrives sooner is answered from memory. guests/get never triggers a listing. Range: 0-3600.

page_size.description: Instances per page of a routine listing (VME default 25). A routine pass walks every page inside one guests/list; a W line reports a pass slower than capabilities.guests_polling_rate. Range: 25-1000.

cold_start_page_size.description: The first listing after the provider starts (RAS is still syncing; nothing routine or cloning runs yet). -1 = the whole fleet in one request (max=-1). 0 = paged like a routine listing. A positive number = that many per request. If VME returns fewer rows than meta.total, or refuses the request, the same listing continues with page_size pages. Range: -1-10000.

max_pages.description: Safety cap on listing pages. Reaching it logs W and switches that refresh to add/update only. Range: 1-1000.

max_drop_ratio.description: Mass-drop guard: a listing that is smaller than the current inventory by more than this fraction is not applied until a second listing confirms it. Range: 0.05-1.

missing_listings_before_drop.description: An instance absent from this many consecutive complete listings is dropped. Protects against offset paging skipping an id while instances are created or deleted. Range: 1-10.

exclude_instance_name_patterns.description: Regular expressions matched against the instance name. A match hides the instance from guests/list.

max_addresses.description: Maximum IPv4 and MAC addresses reported per guest. Range: 1-16.

hide_ip_when_stopped.description: Report no IP for a powered-off guest, even if VME still carries the last address in connectionInfo.

power_action_hold_seconds.description: After a start/stop/suspend this provider issued, how long a listing that still shows the instance's previous power state is not believed: guests/get reports the transition (powering_off / powering_on / suspending) and re-reads that one instance from VME (watch_refresh_interval_seconds) until VME shows the new state. VME can list a stopped desktop as running for tens of seconds; RAS would then see it power back on. 0 = off. Range: 0-1800.

watch_refresh_interval_seconds.description: How often guests/get may re-read (one lean GET) an instance under watch: one with a provider-issued power action pending (power_action_hold_seconds), or a running template in maintenance -- RAS shuts that down through its guest agent on Exit Maintenance, which the listing alone shows up to a polling cycle late. Range: 2-300.

scope._comment: Server-side filters appended to every listing, so instances outside the VDI estate are never downloaded. 0 or empty = off.

hardware._comment: MAC and OS, which exist only on the server object. MACs never change for the life of an instance, so they are learned once per process.

bulk_enabled.description: Learn MAC/OS for the whole fleet with one paged GET /api/servers?vm=true&stats=false after the first listing. false = one GET /api/servers/{id} per instance, on its first guests/get.

bulk_min_interval_seconds.description: Minimum time between bulk passes. Range: 60-86400.

bulk_rerun_missing_threshold.description: Run another bulk pass (subject to bulk_min_interval_seconds) once this many listed instances still have no MAC. Range: 1-100000.

hw_retry_seconds.description: While an instance has no MAC yet (a clone still deploying), how often guests/get may fetch its server object. Range: 5-3600.

cloning._comment: guests/clone and tasks/get. VME returns no id for a clone, so the provider finds it by name.

resolve_method.description: How tasks/get finds a new clone before the next full listing. 'phrase': GET /api/instances?phrase=<name> (small). 'activity': GET /api/activity?name=<name> (experimental). 'list': full listings only. Every candidate is validated (exact name, newer than the submit, not the source, lineage), and a shared full listing every resolve_list_interval_seconds is the safety net in every mode. Allowed: phrase, activity, list.

resolve_list_interval_seconds.description: Minimum seconds between full listings used to resolve clones, shared by every clone in flight. The first one happens this long after the submit. Range: 10-3600.

resolve_timeout_seconds.description: A clone not found this long after the submit fails. Range: 60-7200.

provision_timeout_seconds.description: A clone whose VME status is still provisioning this long after the submit fails. Default = 180 x 10 s minus one minute, so the provider fails with a reason before RAS's own tasks/get budget runs out. Range: 120-14400.

cancel_process_on_giveup.description: When provision_timeout_seconds is reached, also POST /api/processes/{id}/cancel on the clone's newest provision process. Best-effort only -- VME can refuse this ("Process is not cancelable") for exactly the stuck-provision case this targets, so it is not a reliable way to stop the underlying work, only a logged attempt. Failures never change the task outcome.

babysit_window_seconds.description: After tasks/get reported the clone completed, guests/get keeps re-reading it (every tracked_refresh_interval_seconds) and starting it if found off until a real IPv4 appears, for at most this long. A running clone is reported powered_on with or without an IP. Range: 300-86400.

tracked_refresh_interval_seconds.description: A tracked clone is re-read from VME (one lean GET) at most this often. Range: 1-300.

tracked_sweep_max_per_call.description: Other tracked clones re-checked opportunistically per guests/get call. Range: 0-50.

completed_clone_task_output_retention_se.description: How long a completed clone task's clone_id is remembered for a repeated tasks/get. Range: 60-86400.

max_concurrent_clone_operations.description: Most clones allowed unfinished on VME at once, for this provider (every template together): clones RAS is still waiting for, clones reported to RAS early that VME is still provisioning, plus clones the provider gave up on (resolve/provision timeout) that VME has not finished. A guests/clone beyond it is refused at once, without calling VME, so stuck clones cannot pile up on the appliance. A given-up clone frees its slot only when VME confirms it ended (finished, failed or deleted) -- there is no expiry. Caps early completion (linked_clones.early_completion, deploy_event_gate_enabled): with it, linked-clone throughput is about this many clones per VME provisioning time. Default 10, as RAS uses for its other providers. Range: 1-100.

stuck_clone_recheck_seconds.description: While the clone limit is reached, how often the given-up clones are re-checked on VME: one lean GET per clone with a known id, one GET /api/processes?instanceId=<template> per template for clones that never appeared. Refusals in between are answered from memory. Range: 10-3600.

deploy_event_gate_enabled.description: EXPERIMENTAL. Report a clone completed once VME's 'Deploy Virtual Machine' step finished (one GET /api/processes per poll), before provisioning as a whole finished.

template_flapping_workaround_enabled.description: Workaround for an appliance that reports a template's power state inconsistently: always report a Ready template (is_template=true) as powered off with no IP/MAC, unless RAS explicitly started it.

mac_preservation._comment: VME honours networkInterfaces[].macAddress on clone. See docs/MAC-PRESERVATION.md.

enabled.description: When RAS deletes a guest and clones a new one under the same name, request the old MAC for the new NIC. RAS itself does not forward the MAC on a recreate, so this is the only way it survives.

retention_seconds.description: How long a captured MAC waits for a same-named clone. Range: 30-86400.

linked_clones._comment: template_method 'versioning' only (VME 9.1+). Each RAS template version (RAS_TEMPLATE_VERSION_<n>) is one VME snapshot named RAS_TEMPLATE_VERSION_<n>_<template id> plus the linked-clone virtual image VME makes from it (same name). Clones are POST /api/instances with config.imageId. See docs/LINKED-CLONES.md.

snapshot_timeout_seconds.description: How long guests/snapshots/create may take (snapshot process + linked-clone image), and how long guests/snapshots/delete waits for VME to confirm the snapshot gone. Keep below tasks_polling_rate x tasks_polling_retries. Range: 60-14400.

image_wait_seconds.description: After the linked-clone call, how long the virtual image may take to show up in GET /api/virtual-images before the version fails. Range: 10-3600.

image_filter_type.description: filterType for the image lookup by name. VME 9.1 files linked-clone images under 'Synced' (the API default 'User' does not show them). Allowed: synced, all, user, system.

label_images.description: Label each image ras-template-<id> and ras-version-<n> (one PUT /api/virtual-images/{id}, best-effort), so the version map can be rebuilt from VME.

refuse_delete_in_use.description: Refuse guests/snapshots/delete for a version whose image a listed instance still uses (config.imageId). Deleting the snapshot also deletes the image on VME.

early_completion.description: Report a linked clone completed on its first tasks/get, as soon as VME has given it an instance id and not failed it, instead of after VME's whole provisioning (typically 80-90 s). RAS sends guests/clone one at a time and the next only after the previous task completed, so this is what lets clones provision side by side. Held while cloning.max_concurrent_clone_operations clones are still provisioning. A clone that fails after the report is logged E; RAS already counts it as created.

force_stop.description: Send stop as VME's hard power-off (PUT /api/instances/{id}/stop?force=true, VME 9.1+): seconds instead of the guest OS shutdown VME does otherwise (typically 40-60 s). RAS shuts a guest down cleanly through its own agent; a stop it sends the provider is a power-off (its log: 'shutting down guest ... non-gracefully'). Applies to every stop, templates included, and to delete.stop_before_delete. Off: VME's graceful shutdown.

delete._comment: guests/control(delete): one DELETE with force=on, then the id is probed until VME returns 404. guests/list keeps listing it (as powering_off) until then.

stop_before_delete.description: Issue PUT stop before DELETE for a running instance. Off: DELETE with force=on handles a running instance.

keep_backups.description: keepBackups on the DELETE. Off: deleted desktops leave no backup records.

probe_interval_seconds.description: How often a deleting id is re-read (GET, 404 = gone) during guests/list. Range: 1-300.

max_probes_per_list.description: Deleting ids probed per guests/list call, oldest probe first. Range: 1-500.

stuck_after_seconds.description: A deleting instance still running or stopped this long after the DELETE is logged as W. Range: 60-86400.

give_up_after_seconds.description: After this long the id stops being probed and falls back to the normal listing rules. Range: 300-604800.

orphan_detection._comment: Log-only. Flags a clone of a known template that RAS has stopped polling.

check_interval_seconds.description: How often the audit (and the in-memory garbage collection that shares its timer) runs. Range: 30-86400.

stale_poll_after_seconds.description: How long since the last guests/get for an instance before it counts as not polled. Keep well above one full RAS sweep. Range: 60-604800.

logging._comment: See docs/LOGGING.md. E and W lines are always written. Secrets are always masked.

log_level.description: 3 = Standard (lifecycle), 4 = Extended (+ per-operation detail, default), 5 = Verbose (+ every RPC and HTTP call). Accepts the number or 'standard'/'extended'/'verbose'.

log_rpc_bodies.description: At log_level 5, also log the OUT response of every guests/get (otherwise the one-line GUEST summary stands in for it).

log_rotate_max_mb.description: Log size that triggers rotation. Range: 1-2048.

stats_interval_seconds.description: Interval of the I-level call-budget summary (RPCs and VME calls per endpoint, bytes, time). 0 = only at shutdown. Range: 0-86400.

file_exists_check_seconds.description: How often to check the log file still exists at its path -- an external delete (cleanup job, antivirus, a user tidying up) does not fail the next write, so this is what notices and recreates it, logging a W line about the gap. Range: 5-3600.
